intro: If HMRC has made a decision you disagree with, you may be looking for a tax appeal advisor near you to help you challenge it. A tax appeal adviser can guide you through the formal reconsideration process or the First-tier Tribunal, helping you present your case clearly. Telling us what the dispute is about and where you are based lets us introduce you to a suitable UK professional who can quote you directly.
need_heading: What people searching for a tax appeal advisor usually need
need_lead: Most people who search for a tax appeal advisor near me are facing a specific HMRC decision and want local help to challenge it properly.
needs: You have received an HMRC decision you believe is wrong and want to know whether you can appeal it.
You are worried about the appeal deadline and need help getting your challenge in on time.
You have already appealed but HMRC has offered a formal reconsideration and you are unsure whether to accept it or go to the tribunal.
You have evidence and arguments but need help organising them into a clear case.
You want to speak to someone face to face or locally who understands the appeal process and can quote you for the work.
context_heading: The deadline and the reconsideration route
context: Appeals usually have a thirty-day deadline, so it is important to act promptly once you receive an HMRC decision. Missing it can limit your options, so gather your paperwork and seek advice as soon as you can.

A formal reconsideration can resolve some disputes without the need for a tribunal, which may save time and stress. If that does not resolve matters, the First-tier Tribunal is the next step, and your adviser will help you prepare evidence and arguments for either route.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Describe the HMRC decision you want to appeal and the date you received it.
Explain briefly why you think the decision is wrong and what outcome you are hoping for.
Mention whether you have already contacted HMRC or started an appeal.
Say whether HMRC has offered you a formal reconsideration or whether you are heading to the First-tier Tribunal.
Tell us what evidence and paperwork you already have to support your case.
Let us know your location so we can introduce you to a professional near you.
questions: What experience do you have with appeals like mine?
How will you approach my appeal, and would you recommend a formal reconsideration or the tribunal?
What do you need from me to build the strongest case?
How will you keep me informed about deadlines and next steps?
What are your qualifications and are you supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes?
Do you have professional indemnity insurance, and how will your fees be quoted?

faqs.q: Can a tax appeal advisor help if I have missed the thirty-day deadline?
faqs.a: It may still be possible to appeal late in some circumstances, but you should seek advice quickly. An adviser can explain your options and whether you can apply for an extension.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a formal reconsideration and the First-tier Tribunal?
faqs.a: A formal reconsideration is an internal HMRC reconsideration that can resolve some disputes without a tribunal hearing. If it does not resolve matters, you can usually take your case to the First-tier Tribunal.

faqs.q: Do I need to meet my tax appeal advisor in person?
faqs.a: Not necessarily, but searching for someone near you can make it easier to discuss paperwork and evidence face to face. Many advisers also work remotely, so you can choose what suits you.

faqs.q: How do I know a tax appeal advisor is properly qualified?
faqs.a: Tax adviser is not a protected title in the UK, so it is reasonable to ask about qualifications, membership of a specialist body, supervision and professional indemnity insurance before you go ahead.
